thread.title: Texas Department of Transportation urges drivers to avoid distractions behind the wheel
thread.title_full: Texas Department of Transportation urges drivers to avoid distractions behind the wheel

author: N. K. Peak
title: Texas Department of Transportation urges drivers to avoid distractions behind the wheel
text:
The Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) announced on Apr. 1 its continued efforts to reduce distracted driving, urging Texans to keep their focus on the road as part of Distracted Driving Awareness Month.
Distracted driving remains a major concern in Texas, contributing to more than 86,000 traffic crashes last year. TxDOT is highlighting the risks and consequences associated with distractions such as texting, adjusting navigation, or eating while driving.
Dee Davila-Estelle shared her family's experience after a distracted driver hit their vehicle at high speed, resulting in the loss of two children. "The hardest thing a mother has to do is look at her children in coffins," said Davila-Estelle. The Estelle family is now working with TxDOT to remind others about the importance of attentive driving.
TxDOT Executive Director Marc Williams emphasized safe practices for drivers. "When you’re behind the wheel, you should be completely focused on just one thing: driving," said Williams. "Road hazards and obstacles require quick thinking and reaction time, and just a few seconds can be the difference between life and death. I promise that text message or bite of food can wait." The agency is using commercials, billboards, and a mobile exhibit featuring a simulator to educate drivers about these dangers.
State law prohibits reading or sending texts while driving; violators face fines up to $200. As part of its Drive like a Texan initiative—which encourages kindness and responsibility—TxDOT recommends keeping phones out of reach while driving or pulling over safely before handling any distraction.
TxDOT supports economic activity by maintaining an extensive transportation infrastructure across Texas—including highways, traffic signals, and general aviation airports—according to its official website. The department operates under governance from the Texas Transportation Commission and aims to link communities statewide for mobility and quality of life enhancement according to TxDOT. Its multimodal network manages about 556.9 million vehicle-miles traveled daily across both urban and rural areas as reported by TxDOT.
By promoting safe habits through public awareness campaigns like Talk. Text. Crash., TxDOT continues efforts toward reducing preventable accidents caused by distraction.
